crossRefs.note: ‘Your silver and your gold is mine. Your wives also and your children, even the best, are mine.’ ”
He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.
Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
The lofty looks of man will be brought low, the arrogance of men will be bowed down, and Yahweh alone will be exalted…
For there will be a day of Yahweh of Armies for all that is proud and arrogant, and for all that is lifted up; and it…
Therefore it will happen that when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish…
But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly…
The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high, who says…
Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though your nest is set among the stars, I will bring you down from there,”…
He said to him, “Yahweh says, ‘Because you have let go out of your hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction…
He took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.

people.name: Ben-hadad
people.line: King of Aram, contemporary of Asa and Baasha.

people.name: Israel
people.line: Patriarch, son of Isaac, father of twelve tribes

translations.web: So they put sackcloth on their bodies and ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel, and said, “Your servant Ben Hadad says, ‘Please let me live.’ ” He said, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”
translations.bsb: So with sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads, they went to the king of Israel and said, “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please spare my life.’” And the king answered, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”
translations.kjv: So they girded sackcloth on their loins, and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel, and said, Thy servant Benhadad saith, I pray thee, let me live. And he said, Is he yet alive? he is my brother.
translations.asv: So they girded sackcloth on their loins, and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel, and said, Thy servant Ben-hadad saith, I pray thee, let me live. And he said, Is he yet alive? he is my brother.
